question.worked_solution:
The angle ${45}^{∘}$ is special, and its trigonometric ratios have the values

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘}=1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Also, note that ${sin}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2},$ ${cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}$ and  ${tan}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}5{cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}+3{sin}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}-7{tan}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘} & = \\ 5(\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}+3(\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}-7(\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2} & = \\ 5{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}+3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-7(1)^{2} & = \\ 8{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-7 & = \\ 8(\frac{2}{4})-7 & = \\ 4-7 & = \\ -3. & \end{aligned}
$$
